'''Abans PLC''', also known as '''Abans Group''', is a Sri Lankan [[public limited company]] and a diversified [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] in Sri Lanka engaged in [[Information and communications technology|ICT]], [[retail]], manufacturing, logistics, commercial real estate and [[financial services]]. Abans predominantly functions mainly as a consumer retailer selling various electronic appliances, smart phones, laptops, cooking utensils.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abans introduces elegant, durable and multifunctional cookers designed in Europe {{!}} Daily FT |url=https://www.ft.lk/business/Abans-introduces-elegant-durable-and-multifunctional-cookers-designed-in-Europe/34-725133 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.ft.lk |language=English}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Abans launches environmentally sustainable e-waste recovery initiative {{!}} Daily FT |url=https://www.ft.lk/sustainability__environment/Abans-launches-environmentally-sustainable-e-waste-recovery-initiative/10519-705233 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.ft.lk |language=English}}</ref> [[Aban Pestonjee]] is the founder of the Abans Group of companies and serves as the chairperson of the company.<ref>{{cite web | title=Abans makes a difference through its Corporate Social Responsibility efforts | work=Sunday Observer | date=18 March 2023 | url=https://archives1.sundayobserver.lk/2023/03/19/business/abans-makes-difference-through-its-corporate-social-responsibility-efforts }}</ref>

== Corporate history ==
Aban Pestonjee launched her business under the name Abans in 1968 at her home garage, where she managed to restore the used appliances she acquired from auctions and home sales to better working condition and sell them at her corner shop at [[Bambalapitiya]], Galle Road.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Sri Lankan story: Abans Group's journey from corner store to corporate giant {{!}} Daily FT |url=https://www.ft.lk/business/A-Sri-Lankan-story-Abans-Group-s-journey-from-corner-store-to-corporate-giant/34-689270 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.ft.lk |language=English}}</ref> She came up with the idea to launch her own company at a time when Sri Lanka entered into the prospect of a closed economy in the 1960s, which also resulted in the subsequent ban on imports. Aban also took note of how difficult it was to complete household chores through manual labour due to restrictions imposed by Sri Lankan government on importing raw materials and cashed in on the potential by selling secondhand home appliances sourced through embassy auctions.

Abans has facilitated the provision of electrical appliances and electronic items, including air conditioners, televisions, laptops to various beneficiaries, such as local Sri Lankan ministries and departments, by entering into high-value contracts.<ref>{{Cite web |title='Gurubuhuman' by Abans and Education Ministry in Sri Lanka empower teachers |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/print/business/%E2%80%98Gurubuhuman%E2%80%99-by-Abans-and-Education-Ministry-in-Sri-Lanka-empower-teachers/215-272979 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.dailymirror.lk |language=English}}</ref> Abans is officially recognised as the licensed vendor by the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka in terms of telecommunications related services including buying of smart mobile phones.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abans recognised as trusted source for TRCSL-approved smartphones in Sri Lanka - Other {{!}} Daily Mirror |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/other/Abans-recognised-as-trusted-source-for-TRCSL-approved-smartphones-in-Sri-Lanka/117-274907 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.dailymirror.lk |language=English}}</ref> Abans currently serves as the authorised Sri Lankan national distributor for the [[Motorola]] and [[Oppo]] brands while also serves as authorised reseller of [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] iPhones in Sri Lanka.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abans launches Apple iPhone 14 Series in Sri Lanka - Business {{!}} Daily Mirror |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/business/Abans-launches-Apple-iPhone14-Series-in-Sri-Lanka/215-247843 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.dailymirror.lk |language=English}}</ref>

On 21 June 2023, Rusi Pestonjee was appointed as the managing director of Abans with immediate effect following the death of precedent managing director Tito Pestonjee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rusi new MD at Abans {{!}} Daily FT |url=https://www.ft.lk/business/Rusi-new-MD-at-Abans/34-749822 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.ft.lk |language=English}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=bugsbunny |date=2023-06-18 |title=Top businessman Tito Pestongee passed away |url=https://colombogazette.com/2023/06/18/top-businessman-tito-pestongee-passed-away/ |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=Colombo Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref> In October 2023, Abans launched Quick Service at Wellawatte for repairs of appliances such as microwave ovens, irons, blenders, kettles, and water heaters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abans launches 'Quick Service' for on the spot repairs {{!}} Daily FT |url=https://www.ft.lk/business/Abans-launches-Quick-Service-for-on-the-spot-repairs/34-754555 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.ft.lk |language=English}}</ref>

Abans was appointed as the franchisee by the American fast food restaurant [[McDonald's]] in the Sri Lankan context of operating businesses, and the developmental agreement was reached on 21 August 1997, including set franchise terms and conditions. Rusi Pestonjee was also present when Abans reached such a franchise agreement with McDonald's. McDonald's made its entry into the Sri Lankan market in 1998, and since then, Abans has served as McDonald's franchise partner until March 2024.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Colombo HC prevents Abans using McDonald's brand name - Top Story {{!}} Daily Mirror |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/top-story/Colombo-HC-prevents-Abans-using-McDonalds-brand-name/155-279479 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.dailymirror.lk |language=English}}</ref> Abans has also established a long-term partnership with South Korean electronics company [[LG]] for over three decades and has also established over 17 years of strategic alliance with Apple.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abans acclaimed as Most Loved Brand of 2023 in Retail (Lifestyle) category by Brand Finance - Business {{!}} Daily Mirror |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/business/Abans-acclaimed-as-Most-Loved-Brand-of-2023-in-Retail-Lifestyle-category-by-Brand-Finance/215-263239 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.dailymirror.lk |language=English}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Abans displays impressive profit and revenue performance in FY 2020/2021 - Business News {{!}} Daily Mirror |url=https://www.dailymirror.lk/business-news/Abans-displays-impressive-profit-and-revenue-performance-in-FY-20202021/273-213462 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=www.dailymirror.lk |language=English}}</ref>

== Controversy ==
In March 2024, McDonald's removed Abans as their Sri Lankan local partner as part of its global franchise network owing to the poor quality supply of food items and unhygienic food items in McDonald's outlets all over Sri Lanka.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-03-24 |title=McDonald's stores shut in Sri Lanka over poor hygiene case |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/mcdonalds-stores-shut-in-sri-lanka-over-poor-hygiene-case/articleshow/108748051.cms |access-date=2024-03-24 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Yahoo is part of the Yahoo family of brands |url=https://consent.yahoo.com/v2/collectConsent?sessionId=4_cc-session_eb3b495f-2cbe-4c7e-9631-1fafdb08e817 |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=consent.yahoo.com}}</ref> Abans was criticised for failing to meet international hygiene standards when operating the McDonald's outlets in Sri Lanka.<ref>{{Cite web |title=McDonald's Legal Battle: Sri Lanka Stores Closed |url=https://en.wenews.pk/mcdonalds-legal-battle-sri-lanka-stores-closed/ |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=WE News |language=en}}</ref> Around 12 McDonald's outlets in Sri Lanka were closed with immediate effect and McDonald's sign boards were covered up.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-24 |title=12 McDonald's outlets closed in Sri Lanka : Reason revealed |url=https://www.newswire.lk/2024/03/24/12-mcdonalds-outlets-closed-in-sri-lanka-reason-revealed/ |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=NewsWire |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=bugsbunny |date=2024-03-24 |title=McDonald's stores shut in Sri Lanka over poor hygiene case |url=https://colombogazette.com/2024/03/24/mcdonalds-stores-shut-in-sri-lanka-over-poor-hygiene-case/ |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=Colombo Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 24 March 2024, Colombo Commercial High Court issued an enjoining order preventing Abans from using McDonald's name in their business marketing and promotional purposes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-25 |title=McDonald's stores closed in Sri Lanka over poor hygiene: What we know so far |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business/mcdonalds-stores-closed-in-sri-lanka-over-poor-hygiene-what-we-know-so-far-101711331670960.html |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> The Colombo Commercial High Court issued the court order following a lawsuit filed by McDonald's Corporation preventing Rusi Pestonjee, managing director of Abans PLC from any way or manner to use the name McDonald's or any name in any way or manner similar to the name McDonald's.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web | title=McDonald's stores close in Sri Lanka after deal with partner ends | work=Reuters | url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/mcdonalds-stores-close-sri-lanka-after-deal-with-partner-ended-lawyer-says-2024-03-24/ }}</ref>
